_doc: Xuyên Lâm Môn lineage (rules-proposals R5), a no-lean staff-and-footwork school (R3): leans Thunder, Wood -> none. Outer gate: straw-sandal-step-primer (proposal, element-free footwork). Inner gate and above: calm-wind-staff-canon (proposal, Profound, element-free staff). Secret arts: hundred-echo-palm-scripture (existing body technique, inner gate; also the lineage's body art) and unheeding-rain-heart-method (proposal, the head and the Road Mother). Every catalogue staff-like technique runs on an element, so the Gate's are proposals. Unpriced.

lineage.tree_route_note: The guides' walk and the Gate's staff: Willow Dance for footwork, then the Bamboo Joints that make every staff strike quicker and surer.

techniques.name: Straw Sandal Step Primer (Mang Hài Bộ Quyết)
techniques.concept: The guides' first method, learned on the forest road with a load on the back. It draws no element: the student breathes to the rhythm of the step and tempers the legs, the lungs and the soles of the feet, until a day's walk through wet bamboo costs no more than an hour on a dry road. Its forms are walking forms. A primer disciple is hard to knock down and harder to catch.

arts.new: Lighter Than a Horse (Khinh Thắng Mã)
arts.concept: A movement art: for a few seconds you are Pressing, faster and harder to hit; the first time in that window the foe acts, its next art is delayed.

techniques.lore: Written by the founder Mạc Nhất Thoa in 690 for the forest boys who carried travellers' packs (A289). He named it for the line every guide learns before he learns to hold a staff: bamboo staff and straw sandals, lighter than a horse.

techniques.name: Staff Canon of the Calmed Wind and Waves (Định Phong Trượng Kinh)
techniques.concept: The Gate's staff. It cultivates no element; it cultivates steadiness. The cultivator walks while fighting, never stays Composed and never hurries, and each slow step adds weight to the next swing of the staff. Weather, fear and a foe's cries are treated as rain on leaves: heard, and not listened to. It is weak in a single exchange and very strong in a long running fight, which is the only kind of fight a guide has.

arts.concept: A stance kept while moving: each second the holder keeps moving adds a stack; each stack raises the Physical damage of the next staff strike and is spent by it. Standing still for a second, or running (an escape art), loses them all: a guide never runs.
A sweeping staff strike that hits the foe; while the holder has five or more Walk Slowly stacks, it also cleanses one fear or slow status from the holder.
A guard: for a few seconds the fields the foe lays (rain, mist, haze, flood, seals) do not touch the holder, and status effects on them tick at half rate.
A passive art. While you are Pressing, your arts cost less linh lực, and less again for each Walk Slowly stack you hold.

techniques.lore: Mạc Nhất Thoa's own canon, finished in 720. Its nine layers carry the nine lines of the old song the guides sing on the road; the Gate will not say whose song it is.

techniques.name: Heart That Does Not Listen to the Rain (Mạc Thính Tâm Pháp)
techniques.concept: A mind method. It teaches the cultivator to let sound, fear and the pull of another's qi pass through without answer, as rain passes through a forest. In a fight it shuts out soul and song: charms, curses and the soul hits of sound arts lose much of their force on the holder, and the holder's thần thức cannot be read. It is the founder's reply to his lord's teaching: the Tower listens to the rain; the Gate does not.

arts.concept: A passive ward: incoming soul damage and charm statuses are reduced; each one the ward meets in a fight raises it a little further, and the raise fades by a tenth each second that nothing of the kind meets it.

arts.new: Neither Wind Nor Rain (Vô Phong Vũ)
arts.concept: Once per fight, when a status would take control of the holder, it is ignored and the holder's next staff strike cannot miss.

techniques.lore: Taught to the head and to one elder at a time, from master to disciple. Nhậm Bình Sinh walked the forest road on it alone for a month in 907 when the Gate refused the Night Rain arts (A292). The Tower's Hall of Echoes has never heard a word spoken in a room where two of its holders sit.
